source_text: Mortui enim sumus peccato, quomodo adhuc vivemus in illo? Exhibete membra vestra arma iustitiae Deo. Gloria Deo. Amen.
thought_title: Dead to sin, alive to God
orientation: Origen is quoting Paul's words from Romans 6 about the believer's death to sin and call to present their members to God.
pass_a_gloss: Dead [ones] for we are to sin, how still will we live in it? Present [you all] members your [as] weapons of righteousness to God. Glory to God. Amen.

choices.english: For we have died to sin
choices.why: The dative peccato expresses the relation of death to sin; 'died to sin' preserves the dative force and the perfect tense of the state.
rejected: For we are dead to sin

choices.why: The genitive iustitiae is rendered as 'of righteousness' to keep the possessive/qualifying relation explicit.
The imperative is a command to offer or place at disposal; 'present' keeps the active, second-person plural force.
The dative Deo expresses the recipient of glory; 'Glory to God' is the natural English doxological formula.

bible_refs.note: Mortui enim sumus peccato, quomodo adhuc vivemus in illo?
Exhibete membra vestra arma iustitiae Deo

pass_b_english: For we have died to sin; how shall we still live in it? Present your members as weapons of righteousness to God. Glory to God. Amen.
